title: Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe.
phenotype_definition: ageing hallmarks framework (12 hallmarks)
notes: Defines 12 hallmarks: genomic instability, telomere attrition, epigenetic alterations, loss of proteostasis, disabled macroautophagy, deregulated nutrient-sensing, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, stem cell exhaustion, altered intercellular communication, chronic inflammation, dysbiosis. Usable as report section taxonomy.

title: Geroscience: linking aging to chronic disease.
phenotype_definition: geroscience pillars (7)
notes: Seven intertwined pillars (adaptation to stress, epigenetics, inflammation, macromolecular damage, metabolism, proteostasis, stem cells and regeneration; named in full-text Table 1). Coarser alternative taxonomy.

title: Open Genes-a new comprehensive database of human genes associated with aging and longevity.
phenotype_definition: database of genes associated with ageing/longevity
notes: Open Genes: 2402 genes; annotations include hallmarks of aging, longevity associations, gene-ageing confidence level; 6 study types and 12 inclusion criteria. API (open-genes.org) not reachable from sandbox, so per-gene hallmark coverage of v1 genes not measured.

title: Human Ageing Genomic Resources: updates on key databases in ageing research.
phenotype_definition: HAGR database update
n_controls_or_total: GenAge human 307 genes; LongevityMap 3144 variants / 884 genes
notes: Current LongevityMap: 3144 variants / 884 genes, versus the v1 port with 528 rsIDs / 272 genes, so v1 is not the current LongevityMap content. GenAge human: 307 genes.

title: LongevityMap: a database of human genetic variants associated with longevity.
phenotype_definition: LongevityMap database description
notes: Source database of v1. v1 studies.csv carries LongevityMap's significance flag (571 significant, 100 not_significant of 671 rows); v1 has no effect sizes, effect alleles or p-values.

title: GenAge: a genomic and proteomic network map of human ageing.
phenotype_definition: GenAge human ageing genes
notes: Original GenAge description (over 200 entries in 2004).

title: Improving reporting standards for polygenic scores in risk prediction studies.
phenotype_definition: PRS reporting standard (PRS-RS)
notes: 22-item reporting framework (ClinGen Complex Disease WG + PGS Catalog). Requires ancestry of development/validation samples, data source, and method of ancestry inference.

title: The Polygenic Score Catalog as an open database for reproducibility and systematic evaluation.
phenotype_definition: PGS Catalog
notes: Open resource of published scores (variants, alleles, weights) with curated metadata; basis for a 'pgs' pointer table.

title: The Polygenic Score Catalog: new functionality and tools to enable FAIR research.
venue_or_preprint_server: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences (preprint)
phenotype_definition: PGS Catalog update + pgsc_calc
notes: PREPRINT (medRxiv record in PubMed). pgsc_calc implements genetic-ancestry estimation and score normalisation using reference data.

title: Recommendations for risk allele evidence curation, classification, and reporting from the ClinGen Low Penetrance/Risk Allele Working Group.
venue_or_preprint_server: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
phenotype_definition: ClinGen risk-allele classification and reporting
notes: Terminology: Established / Likely / Uncertain risk allele (and protective allele). Report should give classification, zygosity, effect size, and absolute risk when accurate; 'uncertain' only when an assertion with limited evidence exists.

title: Evaluating the Clinical Validity of Gene-Disease Associations: An Evidence-Based Framework Developed by the Clinical Genome Resource.
phenotype_definition: ClinGen gene-disease clinical validity
notes: Definitive / Strong / Moderate / Limited / No Reported Evidence / Conflicting. Mendelian framework; analogy for gene-level evidence, not for common SNP associations.

title: Assessment of cumulative evidence on genetic associations: interim guidelines.
phenotype_definition: Venice criteria: cumulative evidence on genetic associations
notes: Semi-quantitative index on amount of evidence, replication and protection from bias (three levels each), giving strong / moderate / weak credibility.

title: Direct-to-consumer genetic testing: a revised position statement of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics.
venue_or_preprint_server: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
phenotype_definition: ACMG DTC position statement (2016 revision)
notes: PubMed abstract is boilerplate; substantive recommendations not read (full text not retrieved).

title: Statement of the ESHG on direct-to-consumer genetic testing for health-related purposes.
venue_or_preprint_server: European journal of human genetics : EJHG
phenotype_definition: ESHG statement on DTC genetic testing
notes: Clinical utility as essential criterion; pre-test information; counselling; privacy; protect minors; transparent claims.

title: The clinical application of polygenic risk scores: A points to consider statement of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG).
venue_or_preprint_server: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
phenotype_definition: ACMG points to consider: clinical application of PRS (2023)
notes: Title verified only. No abstract in PubMed/Europe PMC; full text not accessible, so content NOT read.

title: Clinical utility of polygenic risk scores for embryo selection: A points to consider statement of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG).
venue_or_preprint_server: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
phenotype_definition: ACMG points to consider: PRS for embryo selection (2024)
notes: Title verified only; content not read.

title: The use of polygenic risk scores in pre-implantation genetic testing: an unproven, unethical practice.
venue_or_preprint_server: European journal of human genetics : EJHG
phenotype_definition: ESHG: PRS in pre-implantation genetic testing
notes: ESHG: utility of PGT-P severely limited and not clinically assessed. Context for what not to claim.

first_author: Polygenic Risk Score Task Force of the International Common Disease Alliance
title: Responsible use of polygenic risk scores in the clinic: potential benefits, risks and gaps.
phenotype_definition: ICDA PRS Task Force: responsible clinical use of PRS
notes: Benefits weighed against uncertainties/biases and misunderstanding or misuse; risk-communication gaps.

title: Polygenic risk scores in the clinic: new perspectives needed on familiar ethical issues.
phenotype_definition: ELSI of clinical PRS
notes: Ancestry-dependent predictive power may exacerbate disparities; role of expert mediators.

title: Clinical genetic counseling and translation considerations for polygenic scores in personalized risk assessments: A Practice Resource from the National Society of Genetic Counselors.
phenotype_definition: practice resource for genetic counsellors on polygenic scores
notes: No consensus on PGS construction and no demonstrated clinical utility yet; limitations must be conveyed.

title: Clinical use of current polygenic risk scores may exacerbate health disparities.
phenotype_definition: PRS accuracy by ancestry
notes: Current PRS several times more accurate in European-ancestry individuals.

title: Polygenic scoring accuracy varies across the genetic ancestry continuum.
phenotype_definition: PGS accuracy along the genetic-ancestry continuum (84 traits)
notes: Accuracy declines with genetic distance (GD) from training data (r = -0.95 averaged over 84 traits); furthest GD decile of Europeans has 14% lower accuracy than closest. Supports a continuous ancestry-distance disclosure.

title: Design and user experience testing of a polygenic score report: a qualitative study of prospective users.
phenotype_definition: user testing of a CAD polygenic score report
notes: Percentiles and word-based risk descriptions best understood; odds ratios removed and colours revised after feedback.

title: Returning integrated genomic risk and clinical recommendations: The eMERGE study.
venue_or_preprint_server: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
phenotype_definition: eMERGE genome-informed risk assessment (GIRA) return
notes: Integrated monogenic + polygenic + family-history + clinical report for 11 conditions.

title: Selection, optimization and validation of ten chronic disease polygenic risk scores for clinical implementation in diverse US populations.
phenotype_definition: eMERGE selection/validation of 10 clinical PRS
n_controls_or_total: All of Us 13,475 used for calibration
notes: Genetic-ancestry calibration of PRS mean and variance; 10 of 23 conditions chosen on performance, actionability, evidence in African and Hispanic populations.

title: Healthcare professionals' experiences returning monogenic, polygenic, and integrated risk results in the eMERGE study.
phenotype_definition: providers' experience returning PRS/IRS (eMERGE IV)
notes: 2026. Confidence: monogenic 92%, PRS 78%, IRS 69%; concerns include interpretation of relative risk.

title: Development and pilot testing of a prostate cancer polygenic risk report.
phenotype_definition: pilot test of prostate cancer PRS patient report
notes: 2026. Pictograph absolute-risk displays aided comprehension; bell curves and incidence curves frequently misunderstood.

title: The development and evaluation of polygenic risk score reports: A systematized review of the literature.
venue_or_preprint_server: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
phenotype_definition: systematized review of PGS report development/evaluation
notes: 2025. Evidence supports absolute risk and avoiding stigmatising colours.

title: Development and evaluation of patient-centred polygenic risk score reports for glaucoma screening.
phenotype_definition: patient-centred glaucoma PRS report
notes: 2025. Pictograph preferred over pie chart and bell curve; absolute risk preferred.

title: Patient Perspectives on Personalized Risk Communication Using Polygenic Risk Scores to Inform Colorectal Cancer Screening Decisions.
phenotype_definition: patient perspectives on colorectal cancer PRS
notes: 2025 qualitative study.

title: Preferences of research participants with experience receiving individual results for future return of results.
venue_or_preprint_server: Journal of clinical and translational science
phenotype_definition: participant preferences after receiving PRS-based results (eMERGE IV)
notes: 2026. 64.9% gave highest importance to receiving results; prefer multiple formats.

title: The impact of communicating genetic risks of disease on risk-reducing health behaviour: systematic review with meta-analysis.
phenotype_definition: effect of communicating DNA-based risk on behaviour
notes: No significant effect on smoking cessation (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.63-1.35), diet or physical activity; no detected adverse psychological effects; low-quality evidence.

title: Genetic essentialism: on the deceptive determinism of DNA.
phenotype_definition: genetic essentialism / determinism bias
notes: Genetic attributions perceived as immutable and determined even for weak genetic explanations.

title: Learning one's genetic risk changes physiology independent of actual genetic risk.
phenotype_definition: RCT: randomised genetic-risk feedback independent of genotype
notes: Being told 'high-risk' vs 'protected' changed physiology and behaviour in a self-fulfilling manner; perceived-risk effects sometimes exceeded actual-genotype effects.

title: Disclosure of APOE genotype for risk of Alzheimer's disease.
venue_or_preprint_server: The New England journal of medicine
phenotype_definition: RCT REVEAL: APOE disclosure to adult children of AD patients
notes: No significant short-term anxiety/depression differences; e4-negative subgroup had lower test-related distress than e4-positive.

title: The impact of direct-to-consumer personal genomic testing on perceived risk of breast, prostate, colorectal, and lung cancer: findings from the PGen study.
phenotype_definition: PGen: DTC genomic results and perceived cancer risk
notes: Measurable but modest, waning change in perceived risk; <4% had large changes.

title: Prescription medication changes following direct-to-consumer personal genomic testing: findings from the Impact of Personal Genomics (PGen) Study.
venue_or_preprint_server: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
phenotype_definition: PGen: medication changes after DTC pharmacogenomics
notes: 5.6% changed medication; <1% unsupervised.

title: Utilization of Genetic Counseling after Direct-to-Consumer Genetic Testing: Findings from the Impact of Personal Genomics (PGen) Study.
phenotype_definition: PGen: genetic counselling uptake after DTC
notes: 4% sought GC; uncertainty about results associated with seeking GC.

title: The general public's understanding and perception of direct-to-consumer genetic test results.
phenotype_definition: public vs genetic counsellor interpretation of sample DTC results
notes: Public rated results easy to understand but often misinterpreted them.

title: False-positive results released by direct-to-consumer genetic tests highlight the importance of clinical confirmation testing for appropriate patient care.
venue_or_preprint_server: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
phenotype_definition: clinical confirmation of DTC raw-data variants
notes: 40% of variants in DTC raw data were false positives; some 'increased risk' calls were benign common variants.

title: Use of SNP chips to detect rare pathogenic variants: retrospective, population based diagnostic evaluation.
phenotype_definition: SNP-chip vs sequencing accuracy (UK Biobank)
notes: Common variants >99% concordant; for variants <0.001% frequency only 16% of 4757 chip heterozygous calls confirmed. PubMed author string 'Mn W'.

title: Third-Party Genetic Interpretation Tools: A Mixed-Methods Study of Consumer Motivation and Behavior.
phenotype_definition: survey of third-party raw-data tool use
notes: 89% downloaded raw data; among downloaders 63% used Promethease.

title: Third party interpretation of raw genetic data: an ethical exploration.
venue_or_preprint_server: European journal of human genetics : EJHG
phenotype_definition: ethics of third-party interpretation websites
notes: Promethease, Interpretome, LiveWello, Codegen.eu, Enlis Personal: questionable validity/utility, inadequate consent, no medical supervision.

title: Impute.me: An Open-Source, Non-profit Tool for Using Data From Direct-to-Consumer Genetic Testing to Calculate and Interpret Polygenic Risk Scores.
phenotype_definition: Impute.me open-source PRS tool
notes: Argues single-SNP reporting that disregards effect size is inappropriate; reports PRS on a population normal distribution.

title: Patient experiences with clinical confirmatory genetic testing after using direct-to-consumer raw DNA and third-party genetic interpretation services.
phenotype_definition: experiences after confirmatory testing of raw-DNA findings
notes: 9/12 raw-DNA P/LP findings not confirmed; distress common.

title: Genetic counseling following direct-to consumer genetic testing: Consumer perspectives.
phenotype_definition: consumers seeking GC after DTC
notes: Consumers want plain-language explanation and a 'game plan'.

title: European citizens' perspectives on direct-to-consumer genetic testing: an updated systematic review.
phenotype_definition: European citizens' views on DTC
notes: Low knowledge, high interest.

title: Helping patients decide: ten steps to better risk communication.
venue_or_preprint_server: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
phenotype_definition: risk communication best practice
notes: Absolute risks as frequencies, pictographs, plain language instead of relative risks.

title: Communicating genetic risk information for common disorders in the era of genomic medicine.
venue_or_preprint_server: Annual review of genomics and human genetics
phenotype_definition: communicating genetic risk for common disorders
notes: Multiple formats, framing, graphics, parsimony, attention to emotions.

title: A meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies identifies multiple longevity genes.
phenotype_definition: survival to >=90th / >=99th percentile age vs controls <=60th percentile
replication_status: APOE replicated (DKLSII, GLS) and validated in UKB parental data; GPR78 not replicated
notes: Only APOE e4/e2 validated in parental-age datasets. Positions in paper are GRCh37.

title: Genomics of 1 million parent lifespans implicates novel pathways and common diseases and distinguishes survival chances.
phenotype_definition: parental lifespan (~1 million parental lifespans)
notes: Polygenic scores show a mean lifespan difference of around five years across deciles; dementia, CVD and lung-cancer variants explain most variance.

title: Multivariate genomic scan implicates novel loci and haem metabolism in human ageing.
phenotype_definition: multivariate healthspan + parental lifespan + longevity
key_loci: 10 shared loci incl. FOXO3, SLC4A7, LINC02513, ZW10, FGD6
notes: Most of the 10 loci associated with cardiovascular disease; haem metabolism pathway.

title: Identification of 12 genetic loci associated with human healthspan.
phenotype_definition: healthspan (age at first major chronic disease)
notes: Healthspan phenotype definition.

title: Genome-wide meta-analysis associates HLA-DQA1/DRB1 and LPA and lifestyle factors with human longevity.
phenotype_definition: parental survival
key_loci: HLA-DQA1/DRB1, LPA new; validated APOE, CHRNA3/5, CDKN2A/B, SH2B3, FOXO3A
notes: MR: +1 BMI unit ~ -7 months lifespan; +1 year education ~ +11 months.

title: Estimates of the Heritability of Human Longevity Are Substantially Inflated due to Assortative Mating.
phenotype_definition: heritability of longevity in Ancestry pedigrees
n_controls_or_total: hundreds of millions of historical persons
notes: Heritability well below 10% after accounting for assortative mating.

title: Quantitative analysis of population-scale family trees with millions of relatives.
phenotype_definition: population-scale family trees
notes: Heritability partitioning from crowd-sourced trees.

title: Heritability of intrinsic human life span is about 50% when confounding factors are addressed.
phenotype_definition: heritability of intrinsic lifespan (twin modelling)
n_controls_or_total: twin cohorts raised together and apart
notes: 2026: intrinsic-mortality heritability above 50% vs 20-25% (twins) and ~6% (pedigrees); heritability claims must name the estimand.

title: The genetics of human ageing.
phenotype_definition: genetics of human ageing
notes: Multi-trait loci link to several age-related diseases; progeria points to genome maintenance.

title: Polygenic prediction of human longevity on the supposition of pervasive pleiotropy.
phenotype_definition: integrated longevity genetic score for exceptional survival
notes: Median lifespan in highest decile of composite index up to 4.8 years longer (author-reported).

title: Depletion of loss-of-function germline mutations in centenarians reveals longevity genes.
phenotype_definition: rare LoF burden in centenarians vs controls
notes: Centenarians 11-22% lower LoF burden; gene-level burden, not array-reportable.

title: Germline burden of rare damaging variants negatively affects human healthspan and lifespan.
phenotype_definition: rare PTV burden and healthspan/lifespan
notes: Rarest PTV burden accounts for 0.4 (healthspan) and 1.3 (lifespan) years of variability.

title: Whole-genome sequencing analysis of semi-supercentenarians.
phenotype_definition: semi-supercentenarians (105+/110+) vs controls
notes: Small n; pathway-level only.

title: FOXO3A genotype is strongly associated with human longevity.
venue_or_preprint_server: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
phenotype_definition: long-lived men vs controls, nested case-control, 5 IIS genes
key_loci: FOXO3A: homozygous minor vs major OR 2.75, P=0.00009
replication_status: later validated at genome-wide level (Joshi 2017; Timmers 2019/2020)
notes: rsID and alleles not stated in abstract; not extracted here.

title: Genetic signatures of exceptional longevity in humans.
phenotype_definition: centenarians vs genetically matched controls; 281-SNP model
notes: Accounts for 280 of 671 (41.7%) v1 studies.csv rows, all flagged 'significant' in v1. 23andMe research blog reported the model appeared overfit in its cohort. Re-analysis after retraction of Science 2010 paper (PMID 20595579).

title: RETRACTED: Genetic signatures of exceptional longevity in humans.
phenotype_definition: exceptional longevity GWAS (retracted)
notes: PubMed publication type 'Retracted Publication'. Zero rows in v1 studies.csv.

title: Western Hunter-Gatherer genetic ancestry contributes to human longevity in the Italian population.
phenotype_definition: centenarians vs controls; ancient ancestry components
notes: 2026: higher Western Hunter-Gatherer-related ancestry in centenarians; ancestry structure is a live confounder in longevity association.

title: Genetic associations with longevity in a Calabrian cohort: an exploratory genome-wide study.
phenotype_definition: long-lived vs younger Calabrians
notes: 2026: APOE and FOXO3 not associated in this isolate; population-specific effects.

title: The Impact of Direct-to-Consumer Genetic Testing on Patient and Provider.
phenotype_definition: DTC impact on patients and providers
notes: Misinterpretation, needless interventions, false reassurance.
